newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eramet sees 1997 nickel broadly balanced.
newsitem.headline: Eramet sees 1997 nickel broadly balanced.

text.p: French mining group Eramet on Tuesday said the nickel market in 1997 should be in balance or in a slight deficit after a small surplus in 1996.

Company projections presented at a press conference tentatively pegged 1997 western world consumption at 907,000 tonnes after 838,000 tonnes in 1996 and supply at 902,000 tonnes after 847,000 tonnes in 1996.
The supply figure was made up of western world production and Russian, Chinese and Cuban exports to the world market.
The event organised by Eramet, which is the world's third single largest nickel producer, preceded a German stainless steel and nickel industry meeting on Wednesday.
Chairman Yves Rambaud said nickel prices had recovered from a sharp fall at the end of 1996 but weakening profitability in stainless steel, the key consumer, could undermine them again.
Nickel prices are now at around 3.50-3.60 cents per lb after a 3.40 cents average in 1996 and 1995's 3.73 cents.
Eramet, which produces nickel, speed steel and manganese, aims to lift nickel output progressively in the next few years.
The 1997 production target is 55,000 tonnes per year (tpy) after 53,413 tonnes in 1996.
Further ahead, it aims at 60,000 tpy by the year 2000, then 65,000 tpy within another two or three years.
Global production in the stainless steel industry, which ccounts for two thirds of nickel use, could rise by five percent in 1997, Eramet said.
But it warned overcapacity could weigh on the industry and sales revenue at stainless steel mills could fall.
Global nickel demand from the stainless sector was forecast to rise by 4.6 percent as oppposed to overall nickel demand growth by 2.5 percent.
Primary nickel supply in 1997 should not grow much in the western world while that from Cuba should rise and that from Russia might fall, Eramet said.
Scrap availability should also be limited.
